lessons.question: A test suite has approved every release you have ever shown it. How useful is it?
options: Useful only if it runs quickly
Doubtful, a useful suite can reveal reasons not to release
lessons.explanation: An evaluation earns its keep by being able to disagree with you. Define acceptable behaviour first, then let the tests find reasons to hold.

lessons.after: Keep development cases separate from final
lessons.prompt: Which set does each use belong to?

items.text: Kept out of agent workspaces during development

lessons.explanation: Development cases are for changing the system; held-out cases stay untouched so the final result is an independent check.

lessons.after: Measure end-to-end task success with a
lessons.question: You attempt 20 cases. 15 succeed, 3 fail and 2 time out. What is the task success rate?
lessons.explanation: Timed-out cases stay in the attempted-case denominator, so 15 / 20 = 75%. Dropping them would give 15 / 18 and flatter the system.

lessons.after: For subjective outputs, write a rubric
lessons.question: Which rubric line could two reviewers apply and agree on?
options: Every numerical claim reconciles to the source rows
lessons.explanation: Observable anchors turn taste into a check anyone can repeat. Vague phrases like good report leave each reviewer guessing.

lessons.prompt: Name a way someone could slip instructions into Harbour's assistant without ever logging in to it.
lessons.answer: Through anything the assistant reads: a ticket, a retrieved page, an uploaded file, a plugin or a saved skill. These are entry points, and content arriving through them is data, not orders.

lessons.after: A threat model identifies assets, actors
lessons.prompt: In Harbour's threat model, is each item something to protect or a way in?
lessons.explanation: Assets are what a failure could damage; entry points are where untrusted content arrives. A threat model maps the paths between them.

lessons.after: Use the T08 fixture to test source content
lessons.question: Which of these tests the system's authority rather than the quality of its answers?
options: Whether the caller can change their own role
lessons.explanation: Authority tests probe what the system lets someone do, such as role changes, restricted documents or actions after cancellation. A well-formatted answer says nothing about those.

lessons.question: The second candidate completes 24 of 30 cases. What is its task success percentage?
lessons.explanation: 24 / 30 = 80%. With no unsafe actions and the rest sent to review, it may suit an assisted pilot if the review workload is affordable.

lessons.question: Why write acceptance criteria before you look at the final results?
options: So the results cannot quietly move the bar
Because it is quicker to write them first
Because the evaluator requires a file to exist
lessons.explanation: Criteria set after seeing outputs tend to bend towards whatever happened. Deciding first keeps the release decision honest.

lessons.after: Run the reference evaluator on a saved
lessons.prompt: Step 1 asks you to inspect evaluator output. What kind of problem is each finding?

items.text: A case in the set has no prediction
The same case ID is predicted twice
A prediction for an ID not in the case set
The right ID with the wrong decision

lessons.explanation: Missing, duplicate and extra IDs break the denominator before accuracy is even measured, so check them alongside wrong labels.

lessons.prompt: Name one failure that should force a hold no matter how high the success rate is.
lessons.answer: For example: a message sent to an unauthorised recipient, a caller changing their own role, a manager-only document retrieved, or an action triggered after cancellation. Boundary failures are reported separately, never averaged away.

lessons.question: Contractual requirements affect your pilot. What should the release record contain?
options: A generic statement that the system is compliant
Nothing, contracts are outside the release record
The appropriate organisational reviewer and their decision
lessons.explanation: You identify who in the organisation must review it and record their decision. Inventing a generic compliance claim would misstate what was checked.
